youtube.title: Storms and the six hour day
youtube.caption:
At a six hour day the Sun races across in three hours and storms are steered four times harder.

Part 5 of 8 of "What If Earth Spun Faster and Couldn't Stop?" — the full video is on this channel.

Sources
1. Storm steering (the Coriolis effect) grows in direct proportion to the spin rate: 23.93 h ÷ 6 h = 4.0 times today, and 23.93 h ÷ 1.4 h = about 17 times. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
2. Speed of the ground at the equator: 1,674 km/h today, 3,340 km/h at a 12 h day, 6,679 km/h at 6 h, 13,358 km/h at 3 h, 20,038 km/h at 2 h, 26,717 km/h at 1.5 h; the Sun is up for half of each day. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
3. Speed of the ground at the equator: one trip around the equator (circumference) divided by the length of the day gives about 1,674 km/h (465 m/s), roughly 1/17 of the speed needed to orbit. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
4. Your weight as a share of what it would be on a non-spinning Earth: 99.7% today, 98.6% at a 12 h day, 94.5% at 6 h, 78.0% at 3 h, 50.4% at 2 h, 11.9% at 1.5 h; a 70 kg person weighs 69 kg at 12 h and 55 kg at 3 h. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
